_README: Provider-published prices read from official pricing pages on 2026-08-27 and adversarially re-verified by a second agent against the same URL. Consumed by scripts/apply_catalog_refresh.py. Each entry states the unit EXPLICITLY because the #1 error mode is a unit mismatch (a per-image figure compared against a per-1M-token figure looks like a 160x price change).

price_corrections.evidence: FAQ verbatim: 'API usage is billed in US dollars, not credits. Text to Speech $0.10 per 1,000 characters (v2/v3) or $0.05 (Flash/Turbo).' $/1K identical in all six plan columns. Cross-check: Creator $22 / 220,000 chars = $0.10 per 1K exactly.
price_corrections.why_we_were_wrong: Our 91.65 was derived on the CREDITS basis (0.5 credits/char). The API is billed in USD, not credits, so the derivation used the wrong basis and overstated cost by 83%.

price_corrections.evidence: Priced on the same 'Flash / Turbo' product card at $0.05 per 1,000 characters.

confirmed_correct_no_change.evidence: Footnote: 'Image output is priced at $30 per 1,000,000 tokens. Output images up to 1024x1024px consume 1290 tokens and are equivalent to $0.039 per image.'
$120.00 per 1M image output tokens = $0.134 per 1K/2K image. Catalog matches source exactly.
$60.00 per 1M image output tokens = $0.067 per 1K image. Catalog matches source exactly.
$30.00 per 1M image output tokens = $0.0336 per 1K image. Catalog matches source exactly.

scope_warnings_do_not_apply_eol.why_not_applied: The deprecation entry names the DATED SNAPSHOT (gpt-5-2025-08-07 etc.), NOT the bare alias. The bare aliases still carry live, unannotated pricing rows. eol_date is an ACTIVE SWITCH (selector._is_eol drops any row on/after the date), so writing the snapshot's date onto the alias would disable a model that may still be serving. Left unset deliberately; revisit before 2026-12-11.
scope_warnings_do_not_apply_eol.note: gpt-5-mini and gpt-5-nano ALREADY carry eol_date 2026-12-11 in the catalog from a previous refresh - flagged for review, not changed in this pass.

unit_defects_flagged_not_changed.provider_basis: $0.50 per 1M input TEXT TOKENS, $10.00 per 1M output AUDIO TOKENS. Footnote: 'Audio tokens correspond to 25 tokens per second of audio.'
unit_defects_flagged_not_changed.why_not_changed: Genuine unit mismatch, but converting characters to audio-seconds needs a speech-rate assumption our catalog does not encode. Correcting it blind would swap one wrong number for another. Filed for a dedicated fix.
unit_defects_flagged_not_changed.rough_direction: At ~15 chars/sec, 1M chars is ~66,667s ~ 1.67M audio tokens ~ $16.67 per 1M chars, i.e. we may be UNDERSTATING by ~2x.

unit_defects_flagged_not_changed.provider_basis: $0.60 text input / $12.00 audio output. Two reads of the same page disagreed on tokens vs characters; the VALUES were stable.
unit_defects_flagged_not_changed.why_not_changed: Unit unresolved at source. Value matches the audio-output figure either way, so the ranking input is not obviously wrong.

reverted_plan_dependent.why_reverted: Inworld pricing is PLAN-DEPENDENT and the catalog row records our plan: 'Per-plan: Creator $30/M / Developer $25/M / Growth $20/M. We are on Creator so $30/M applies.' The research read the $25 on-demand/pay-as-you-go rate, which is a DIFFERENT basis. Contrast ElevenLabs, where the researcher explicitly verified the API rate is identical across all six plan columns - that is why the EL correction stands and this one does not.
reverted_plan_dependent.to_resolve: Confirm the current Inworld plan in the Inworld console billing page, then set 30.0 (Creator), 25.0 (Developer) or 20.0 (Growth).

verified_but_deliberately_not_applied.evidence: Pricing page shows $4.00 in / $20.00 out. Footnote verbatim: 'GPT-5.6 Sol's promotional pricing is available at least through November 21, 2026.'
verified_but_deliberately_not_applied.caveat: PROMOTIONAL and SHORT-CONTEXT ONLY. Verifier catch: the $4.00 row is the <272K-context column; prompts over 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and 1.5x output for the full request, and we advertise a 1,050,000-token window. Believed list price $5/$30 was NOT found on an official page - treat as unverified.
verified_but_deliberately_not_applied.status: NOT APPLIED - promotional price must not re-tier a frontier row
verified_but_deliberately_not_applied.why_not_applied: cost_per_unit drives frontier tiering. $4.00 drops gpt-5.6-sol below the $5 frontier boundary, collapsing the frontier set to {ANTHROPIC} (provider monoculture, Tenet-1 concern) and lifting DEFAULT_WILLINGNESS_TO_PAY_USD 3.00 -> 4.00, which widens the cost normalisation band every cheap tier is scored under. A 12-week discount is not a durable cost structure. Re-check 2026-11-21 - if $4/$20 becomes list, change it WITH the frontier boundary.
